title: FIG. 04 · The handover ledger
summary: One full-width ledger on one paper surface: the six assets in their three capability groups, each striking out one of the six problems from your letter and replacing it with what changes, completing one row at a time, in 997px instead of 1,296.
story: The letter's payoff: the six problems it listed are struck out in the same words and order by the six assets that end them, so this act closes with the reader holding documents. That exit hands straight to the method, which shows where the work starts and marks the same Handover line on its track.
motion: Standalone (done by about 4.9s): the heading rises as on every section, with the thin rule above it drawing in, and the red rule and paragraph arrive at the right. The ledger's rules draw left to right, the Handover line drops down through the table, and its red flag and name appear. Then the six rows rise in as drafts: dashed document outlines, the six problems from the letter still unstruck, and the After column empty.

Then the rows complete one by one, 01 to 06, one every 0.42s. A pale band passes over each row as it is posted. The document's outline is redrawn solid as its dashes fade, and its page fills in. The old problem is struck by a drawn hairline and greys out, the arrow on the Handover line darkens, and the new line slides out from the Handover line into the After column. After the sixth row, the title block (Yours 06/06) appears.

On the homepage, the heading and the draft rows arrive when the section scrolls in. The rows only start completing once the ledger itself is well in view (60% visible), so nothing completes below the fold. It plays once and nothing loops.

Hovering a row tints it and darkens its document's outline. With reduced motion, on phones, or with scripts off, the finished state shows at once: every outline solid, every problem struck, every after in place.
addressed: 'I don't like the way things are laid out… especially the black bar kind of thing on the top': the dark side column is gone completely. The section is one surface, edge to edge, and all of it is paper, your side. Kelwin now appears only as the dashed draft outlines, which turn solid as each asset becomes yours.

'It's making the main content of the section take up too much vertical space': the section is 997px tall instead of 1,296, about a quarter shorter. On a normal laptop screen the heading and all six rows fit on one screen. The paragraph moved up beside the headline, and the six assets are now one dense ledger instead of a tray of large sheets.

What you approved is kept: the same headline and paragraph, and the six assets in their three capability groups with their tags. The six problems from your letter are struck word for word, with the same numbers. The handover test and the dashed (Drafted by Kelwin) to solid (Owned by you) key also stay, and the key now sits directly above the documents it explains.

Your standing note that artifacts must be clear at first glance: each row reads left to right in one pass. It gives the asset, then the problem it ends (struck), an arrow across the Handover line, then what replaces it. The rows complete one at a time in that same order, so the motion teaches the reading.

Your note on repeated layouts: there is no panel, caption strip or toggle. The heading is also laid out differently from its neighbours, with the headline on the left and the paragraph bottom-right, as in the hero. So it repeats neither the centred poster above nor the method's heading below.
notes: Surface: paper. The principle above is paper and the method below is graphite. Paper keeps the whole section on his side, so dashed means Kelwin's draft and solid ink means his. It also lets this section mark both of its own seams: .ac-sec--ruled draws the paper-to-paper hairline under the principle, and the method is a hard surface cut. A graphite handover would run into the graphite method with no cut (method S, V and W all lack .ac-sec--ruled), and it would put two vertical 'Handover' datums in one dark field. On paper they rhyme across a surface change instead. If the method round-4 pick is the 'Phase ledger' (method W), two tables would sit back to back with only the surface change between them. Pairing this with method V, or handover V with method W, avoids that. Height: 997px at 1440 (round 3: 1,296). Padding is 128 at the top and 112 at the bottom; the 16px went to the head-to-ledger gap to stay at or under 1000. Layout: the head is the kit .ac-head with the statement on cols 1–7. The red rule and lede sit in a wrapper on cols 8–12, bottom-aligned so the lede's last baseline sits on the statement's (measured within 1px in both skins). Because they are not direct .ac-head children, their entrance is re-timed locally to the kit's 520 and 600ms. The ledger runs on cols 1–12: Capability (1–2) · No. + 28×40 FOLIO glyph + asset name (20px Mona 500) over its .ac-cap tag (3–5) · Before, struck (6–8) · the Handover datum on the 8|9 gutter, with an 18px arrow centred on it · After (9–12). The row is a 10-column grid on cols 3–12, so every cell sits on the page grid. Name, index, before and after share one baseline (within 1px in both skins). Glyph kinds are the round-2 assets X page furniture redrawn at 28×40: hierarchy, bullets, table with a live cell, if→then rules, two readout panels, quarter ticks. There are no rings, fields or nested corners. Strikes are SVG <line>s (not text-decoration) inside each before's inline-block, using x2=100%, so they fit either skin's text width with no measuring. They draw by scaleX. The solid glyph edge is a pathLength=1 path plotted round. The red: the datum's 2×12 flag only, plus family punctuation (two label squares and the head rule). Words added beyond the fragments are column labels only: 'Capability', 'No.', 'Asset', 'Before · Without the system' and 'After · With the system' (both from beforeafter X). There are no numbers, years, clients or results. The title block reads 'Fig. 04 | Handover | Yours 06/06 | Specimen'. 'Specimen' covers the illustrative document glyphs; 'Yours 06/06' is the static end cap, not a counter. When armed it arrives whole after row 06, so there is never an empty cell. Motion: all timing lives in CSS. W.js only adds .is-arm (opening state) and .is-run (start). Standalone sets both at once, with --hw-t0 1600ms and --hw-cad 420ms. On the homepage an IntersectionObserver on the ledger (threshold .6) starts the run, with t0 = max(300, 1200 − time since the section arrived). With no JS, reduced motion or ≤760px nothing is armed, and the default CSS is the final state. All keyframes use fill 'backwards', because every end state equals the default CSS. Capture bug found and fixed: mk's full-height screenshot briefly re-evaluates the ≤760px query, so any display:none toggle there restarted entrance animations and showed blank elements in the shot. The phone rules therefore hide the header row, datum, arrows and cursor with visibility or clip, never display:none. Phone (≤760px): the head stacks at 44px with the key above the bands. Each row becomes a short card: index, glyph, name and tag, then the struck before and the after indented under the name. There are no column heads, datum or sequence, and the title block fits one line at 358px. Copy sources: assets X (names, tags, grouping, key, datum), beforeafter X (befores, afters, column labels, 'Same team, same market'), letter S (the six margin lines and indices), FAQ X Q04/Q05, FirmAbout.tsx ('Each quarter deposits into the next'). All ★ lines are unchanged.
